body:
Index for the 2026-09-26 performance and technical-debt audit (Claude), at `3a3846fd`.
The Stars texture was excluded (another session owns it).
It ran alongside Codex's audit, #1171 (issues #1172–#1177), which Yan ran for comparison.
The two overlap little: Codex went deep on the audio thread, tuning state, motion and the export CLI, and this audit went broad across GPU, build, CI, docs and the take format.
Everything found is filed below.
This issue holds what does not belong in any one of them: the method, the measured frame breakdown, and a "checked and healthy" list so the next audit can skip it.

## Method

Six parallel read-only auditors (Opus), one per slice: the lattice GPU pipeline, the spectral GPU pipeline, UI per-frame CPU, scene/core/analysis, plugin/record/offline, and build/CI/docs/dead code.
Each was given the #317 and #895 "checked and healthy" lists and the settled decisions.
Each issue marks which claims were re-verified by hand, which were measured, and which are an auditor's static reading.
Static estimates are labelled ESTIMATED with their arithmetic; expect some to shrink under measurement.

**A known gap: this audit missed #1172.**
The brief listed "audio thread" as already healthy from #895.
That list covered locks, allocation and logging, not algorithmic cost, and the plugin auditor skimmed the Hub's confirm path.
A future brief should scope inherited "healthy" lists to what was actually checked.

## Where the frame goes (measured)

**Setup:**
- Offline renderer, release build at `3a3846fd`, rendering `take-2026-09-11_03-56-10` (a real 83 s performance with audio), song time 30–50 s, 600 frames at 30 fps.
- Yan's live look read from the newest Bitwig project: Stars texture, Clouds material, Gaussian shadows in all four groups, colour memory on.
- Frames were piped to a discarded raw stream, so x264 is out of the loop.
- Seven variants × two sizes × three rounds, with the order rotated each round.
  Each cost is the median of per-round differences from the Mosaic baseline.
- Load average ranged from 8 to 25; round 0 was inflated everywhere, and rounds 1–2 agree.
- `readback` is the export loop's wait for the GPU, including the frame copy.

| | 1920×1080 | 3840×2160 |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPU: `ui+tess` | 0.7–0.9 ms | 1.0–1.2 ms |
| CPU: `submit` | 1.3–1.8 ms | 1.3–1.9 ms |
| GPU, Mosaic in place of Stars | 8.7 ms (6.4–13.2) | 12.2 ms (quiet rounds 12.1, 12.2) |
| + Stars (the live look) | **+9.9** (+5.0 to +12.9) | **+13.9** (+9.0 to +31.9) |
| − spectrogram (heatmap, Mosaic clouds, memory) | **−2.0** (−2.6 to −1.4) | **−2.9** (quiet rounds −2.9, −3.0) |
| − all shadows (depth 0 in all four groups) | **−1.9** (−2.7 to −0.8) | unresolved (−0.7 to +6.9) |
| − roll | −1.0, unresolved | −0.5, noise |
| − glow and bloom | +0.3, noise | −0.5, noise |
| − lattice atmosphere | +0.9, noise | +0.5, noise |

**Reading it:**
- The export frame is **GPU-bound, three to ten times over**.
- Stars is more than half the GPU time in the live look.
- Of the rest, only **the spectrogram and shadows** clear the noise (deltas under about 1 ms are not resolvable here).
- Shadows at 4K need a quiet-machine rerun.
- This is the export path: the live plugin overlaps CPU and GPU and shares the GPU with Bitwig's own drawing.

**Also measured:** a commit that changes no code costs a **34 s** release rebuild of perf, ui, offline and plugin (#1180).

## Recommended order

**First, from #1171:** #1172 (the audio-thread confirm republication).
For a plugin, an audio-thread cost outranks every frame-time item.

**Quick wins** (small, mostly verified, no picture change):
- #1180: build tag in leaf crates, unused dependencies.
- #1181: CI's unasserted Gaussian sweep and stale gate.
- #1197: PATCHES.md is missing a vendor patch; skills contradict AGENTS.md.
- #1185: **remove VST3** (decided by Yan).

**Fix the instruments before the next GPU optimization:** #1182 (the lattice probes over-count off-pane instances about 8×; the spectrogram probe silently measures memory ON).

**GPU, probe first:**
- #1183: colour memory format and sizing; about 0.9 ms at 4K ESTIMATED.
- #1184: the shared shader module (editor open), and per-style entry points without the Stars arm.
- #1186: #1164's local shadow pass, part of the measured shadow cost.
- #1187: small exact shader wins and dead lanes; bundle with a corpus regeneration.

**Correctness:**
- #1195: the missing-history banner never clears (verified; needs a call on what it means).
- #1189: halo margin at pane edges (not seen in use; one probe).

**Debt:**
- Hand-maintained contracts: #1190 (spectral), #1188 (lattice).
- Duplicated code: #1192 (naming), #1193 (widgets).
- #1196: dead API.
- #1194: take density and per-record flush.
- #1191: dense-window CPU, beside #1175.

**Docs:**
- #1197: guidance (most-read, fix first).
- #1198: delete finished plans.
- #1199: stale facts.
- #1200: stale comments.

## Checked and healthy: do not re-audit

- **Lattice:**
  - #691's tiled gather is gone (#877 splats, #879 half resolution).
  - #995 items 4 and 5 landed.
  - No per-frame bind group, view or texture churn.
  - Every lattice target key is narrow in both directions.
  - `GpuTimer` never waits.
  - The four-target scene split is load-bearing.
  - The Contours/Interference materials (#1168) run only where there is light.
- **Spectral:**
  - The heatmap upload is one slab per frame; `4a4ae66` has not regressed.
  - `TileKey` and `memory_key` are correct in both directions today (#1190 is about the next dial).
  - Memory ping-pong and shift maths are right.
  - No retired-dial residue.
  - The tone target is live above 2 ppp.
  - The roll bloom is region-sized and skipped with no notes.
  - #529's dirty-band publish is not worth building.
  - The duplicated WGSL helpers (`linear_from_gamma_rgb` ×3, two fullscreen-triangle vertex shaders) are stable and not worth churn.
- **UI:**
  - #895 decision 2's cheap half landed.
  - The `FoldedGrid`/`RunKey` and `ShadeLut` keys are sound.
  - `SpectrogramAgg` is incremental.
  - `names::plan` is bounded.
  - No dead ui `pub` items; no persisted field lacks a reader.
  - `names.rs` is large because of its tests (369 code lines), not dead code.
- **Core, analysis and scene:**
  - #995 items 9 and 10 landed (#1016).
  - `SpectrumHistory` push is amortized O(1).
  - `NoteRoll` scans cost about 10–20 µs, so no index is needed.
  - The `TrailField` index is fine.
- **Plugin, record and offline:**
  - #995 items 7, 8 and 11 and #895 decision 1 all landed.
  - `process()` is 8 atomic loads per block with no allocation.
  - Hub buffers are pre-sized; the exception is #1172's confirm path.
  - The export's frame buffers are recycled.
  - RGBA→YUV on the GPU is not worth it (≤3% of an encoder-bound export).
  - Readback pipelining is #660, deferred.
- **Tree:**
  - Zero TODO/FIXME.
  - Three `allow(dead_code)`, two of them justified.
  - `unsafe` carries SAFETY comments.
  - No realistic host-data panics.
  - All Cargo features are enabled somewhere.
  - `cargo tree -d` duplicates are all upstream.
  - Profiles are sound.
  - The metal-assets build.rs is keyed correctly.
  - Every numbered PATCHES.md patch is still present.
  - CI sccache hits about 98%.

comments.body:
Non-cloud issue sweep completed. Thirteen PRs were reviewed as warranted, rebased and merged sequentially after final-head Full CI and CLEAN merge state; shader changes also carried verified Metal assets. Both plugin and offline release packages were built for every plugin-affecting branch. Cloud-labeled issues remained with the other session.

| PR | Result / issue coverage |
| --- | --- |
| #1206 | Departing marks follow octave-sector timing; closes #1204. |
| #1207 | Correct live-window and memory timing workloads/brackets; partial #1182. |
| #1208 | One complete confirmed-pitch snapshot per callback and batch validation; closes #1172, #1173; part of #1196. |
| #1209 | Leaf build tags and unused direct dependency removal; partial #1180. |
| #1210 | Selective sparse halo owners without exceeding the node cap; closes #1189. |
| #1211 | Once-per-writer-pass take flushing with error accounting; partial #1194 and #1196. |
| #1212 | Preserve pane sizes across folds and refused resizes; closes #1154. |
| #1213 | One scene/transmittance pass and shared lattice pipeline construction; closes #1186, #1188; partial #1187. |
| #1214 | Remaining dead runtime APIs and offline alignment override removed; closes #1196. |
| #1215 | Timer ends at the actual dependent preparation pass; closes #1150; partial #1182. |
| #1216 | Shared lazy per-frame note naming; closes #1192. |
| #1224 | Shared spectral shader construction, uniform/key contracts, bucketed color-history allocation and full-depth shortcut; closes #1184, #1190; partial #1183. |
| #1226 | Joined CLAP teardown completes an already stopped, complete take; partial #1225. |

No PR from this sweep remains unmerged. Existing evidence-only #1170 is outside this sweep and remains open.

Remaining non-cloud items:
- #1039 and #886: owner elected to wait for a reproducible saved view/take.
- #1220: owner must choose which visual idea, if any, to pursue.
- #1194: real 60-second expressive recording and fast-export density/parse measurements remain; no format/coalescing change is justified yet.
- #1225: Stop while deactivated but kept alive still waits for processing; the destruction path is fixed, and the separate lifecycle/liveness case remains.
- #1182: separate host-draw timer overhead remains unmeasured; workload/bracket and lattice-timer fixes are done.
- #1180: hot-reload opt-in remains an unmeasured development-default change. PNG rewrite was declined because image remains transitive.
- #1187: slot-trig tables remain unmeasured. CPU glow constants changed exact goldens, and separating dead padding lanes saved no bytes; both were rejected.
- #1183: retain F32 because F16/UNORM convergence changed release by frame rate; region cropping's roughly 0.3 ms bound does not currently justify added history/coordinate machinery.
- #1219: recommend retaining the simpler ordered release loop; no material typical-chord gain justifies reshaping shared release ownership.
- #1142 and #1201 remain research/index trackers, not finished implementation work. #1178 was already completed by #1202 before this sweep.

The broad halo-window expansion was rejected (about 60–63% more nodes and a broken cap). The merged selective design added about 4–15% at default tested views, matched padded-reference pixels, and showed no consistent GPU regression. Views already at the cap cannot add halo owners.

Per-style spectral splitting missed its prescribed measured-win threshold, so that extra pipeline complexity was not shipped. No merge audit was started; the combined batch is worth an owner-invoked audit.
Closing: every indexed issue is closed except #1142, which is tracked on its own. The frame breakdown and the checked-and-healthy list stay here for the next audit to link.
